title: Add Amp extension
body:
## Description

Adds **Amp** — create and track [Amp](https://ampcode.com) threads from Raycast. Threads run remotely in Amp Orbs.

- **New Thread** — prompt, Amp Cloud project, mode, visibility, and file attachments; opens the created thread in the browser by default, or starts it in the background / opens a terminal / copies the URL or CLI attach command
- **Capture Window and Start Thread** — screenshots the frontmost window and attaches it to a new thread (assign a global hotkey for one-keystroke capture)
- **My Threads** — browse all threads: open, copy URL, change visibility, copy attach command, open in terminal
- **Amp Threads** — root-search overview row with live running/unread counts
- **Amp Thread Status** — menu bar icon with running and unread counts, refreshed every minute

Requires the Amp CLI to be installed and logged in (`amp login`); setup is covered in the README. Screenshots are in `metadata/`.

## Screencast

Screenshots included in `metadata/` (form with actions, thread list with actions, menu bar dropdown).

## Checklist

- [x] I read the [extension guidelines](https://developers.raycast.com/basics/prepare-an-extension-for-store)
- [x] I read the [documentation about publishing](https://developers.raycast.com/basics/publish-an-extension)
- [x] I ran `npm run build` and [tested this distribution build in Raycast](https://developers.raycast.com/basics/prepare-an-extension-for-store#metadata-and-configuration)
- [x] I checked that files in the `assets` folder are used by the extension itself
- [x] I checked that assets used in the `README` are located outside the metadata folder if they were not generated with our [metadata tool](https://developers.raycast.com/basics/prepare-an-extension-for-store#how-to-use-it)
